Stealth CMEs are defined as CMEs originating on the visible solar disk without associated X-ray flares above class B1.0 or filament eruptions.
The study period is from 2008 to 2014, during which 6850 CMEs were recorded by LASCO, 7809 by COR2A, and 9529 by COR2B.
A total of 96 stealth CMEs were identified after applying exclusion criteria.
The angle φ between CME motion in the ecliptic plane and the Sun–Earth line is used to determine the CME's solar origin side; |φ| ≤ 90° indicates the visible side.
The angle λ measures the CME motion direction relative to the ecliptic plane in 3D space.
Stealth CMEs have the lowest average velocity, kinetic energy, mass, and angular size among the three CME groups studied.
The relative frequency of stealth CMEs peaked around 2011 near solar minimum and declined during solar maximum years 2013–2014.
Triangulation methods using simultaneous observations from SOHO LASCO and STEREO SECCHI coronagraphs were employed to reconstruct CME 3D kinematics.
CMEs associated with X-ray flares and/or filament eruptions are grouped as FSCME with LCS.
The study excludes CMEs originating on the far side of the Sun (|φ| > 90°) due to uncertainty in associating them with low coronal signatures.
The distribution of CME central position angles (CPA) correlates linearly with the angle λ, showing propagation latitude trends.
Stealth CMEs tend to cluster near φ = –50° in longitude, while FSCME with LCS cluster near φ = 50°.
The velocity distribution of stealth CMEs peaks near 300–350 km/s, lower than that of other CME groups.
The study uses catalogs of solar flares and filament eruptions to exclude CMEs linked to these phenomena.
The generation mechanism of stealth CMEs is hypothesized to differ from typical CMEs triggered by filament eruptions, but remains unclear.
The authors developed an automated procedure to select stealth CMEs from large CME datasets.
Relative frequency distributions of CME parameters show bell-shaped or parabolic forms depending on the parameter.
Changes in the angle φ with distance from the Sun were analyzed to study CME motion evolution.
The study confirms that stealth CMEs have smaller angular sizes compared to other CME groups.
The study's triangulation method is based on earlier work by Egorov and Fainshtein (2021).
